title: The fall of Constantinople
subject: histoire
description: On May 29, 1453, after 53 days of siege, the Ottomans forced the walls of Constantinople. New Rome falls, and the Middle Ages change.

hero.hook: A thousand years of ramparts. Fifty-three days of cannons. A city that closes an era.

blocks.text: On **May 29, 1453**, after **53 days** of siege, the soldiers of the Ottoman sultan entered **Constantinople**, capital of the Byzantine Empire (the Eastern Roman Empire). The city which had resisted for more than a millennium gave way under the blows of new artillery.
It's not just the end of Byzantium. By blocking the routes to the East, the fall of “New Rome” pushed Europe to look for other paths. The Middle Ages are closing.

Founded in **330** by Emperor Constantine, the city was for a long time the beacon of Europe. In the 15th century, the Byzantine Empire was nothing more than a shadow, weakened above all by : Christian crusaders from the West had plundered the city. There remains the capital and some Greek territories. About **50,000** people live among the ruins, where there were once **500,000** souls. [[The sack of Constantinople by the 4th Crusade (1204)]]

blocks.caption: The Theodosian walls, long considered impregnable.

blocks.text: Its last asset: the , triple line of ramparts from the 5th century. For a thousand years, no one forced them through the earth. Constantinople is a Christian island in an Ottoman sea. [[Theodosian Walls]]
Even when surrounded, the Byzantines continued to argue over tiny theological points. The expression “Byzantine discussion” stuck.

In **1451**, **Mehmed II**, young sultan of the Ottoman Empire, is **19 years old** and has an obsession: taking the City. He hired the founder **Urban**, who forged the “Basilica”, a **8 meters** cannon firing **600 kg** cannonballs. Medieval fortifications are becoming obsolete.

blocks.caption: Mehmed II, the young sultan who wants Constantinople.

blocks.text: The siege begins on **April 2, 1453**. Faced with **80,000 to 200,000** Ottomans, including the  (sultan's elite troops), the last Byzantine emperor  only fielded **7,000** defenders. Every night, they will fill in the gaps with wood and earth. [[Janissaries]] [[Constantine XI Palaiologos]]
Urban's cannon was so heavy that it took **60 oxen** and **400 men** to move it. He could only shoot **7 times** per day, otherwise he would explode.

Blocked at , the city's natural port, by a chain stretched across the water, Mehmed had **70 ships** towed by land behind the defense. **29 May**, at dawn, the general assault carried a breach near the Saint-Romain gate. We also talk about a small door, the **Kerkoporta**, left open. [[Golden Horn]]

Constantine XI throws himself into the fray; his body will never be formally identified. Mehmed converted **Hagia Sophia**, the great basilica, into a mosque. Constantinople becomes , capital of a conquering empire. [[Istanbul]]

blocks.text: Greek scholars flee to Italy with their manuscripts: . On the commercial level, the Ottomans heavily taxed the routes to the East. Portugal and Spain seek the Atlantic. In **1492**, Columbus stumbles upon America. [[The Greek diaspora and the Renaissance]]

The fall puts an end to the living continuity of the : for a thousand years, Constantinople had transmitted Roman law and Greek culture. Modern Europe was born in part from this mourning: a thousand-year-old empire died out, another world opened up. [[Byzantine law and Roman heritage]]
**May 29, 1453**, Constantinople falls after a thousand years of resistance. End of Byzantium, Ottoman rise, acceleration of the Renaissance and the Great Discoveries: a pivotal date.
